training.heading: Training, exam and certification: how they fit together
training.intro: Most enquiries mix up three different things. Knowing which one you need makes the quote accurate and the enrolment quick.

stages.p: Classroom and practical hours in one method (UT, MT, PT, RT, VT, ET, PAUT or TOFD) at Level I or Level II. ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum hours per method and level; your employer's written practice sets the hours that actually apply to you.
stages.you: A course, practical time on specimens and a record of hours for your certification file.

stages.p: General, specific and practical examinations, set and graded under the employer's written practice by, or under the direction of, an NDT Level III.
stages.you: Exams administered and graded, with the papers and results kept for the employer's records.

stages.p: Under SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 your employer certifies you, on the evidence of training, experience hours, exams and a vision test. A training provider cannot certify you on its own. Under ISO 9712 schemes such as PCN, a third-party body certifies.
stages.you: Everything your employer's Level III needs to sign the certification, or a route to an employer-based programme if your company does not have one.

training.prereqHeading: Prerequisites to check before you enrol
prereqs: Vision: a near-vision acuity check, normally every year, plus a colour-contrast check set by the written practice.
Experience hours in the method: certification needs logged on-the-job hours as well as classroom hours. Training alone is not enough.
Level order: Level I before Level II, unless the written practice allows the combined hours to go straight to Level II.
The written practice: if your employer has one, it decides hours, exams and who signs. If not, see written-practice support under Level III consulting.
